result: Background claims establish that placental malaria (PM) is most severe in first pregnancies, results from VAR2CSA-expressing parasites binding CSA in the placenta, and that women develop protective anti-VAR2CSA antibodies over successive pregnancies. VAR2CSA is described as a large multidomain protein that is the leading PM vaccine candidate.
evaluation: These claims (C1-C28) represent well-established background knowledge supported by multiple citations to prior literature. They provide the scientific context for the study but are not novel findings from this work. The claims are consistently supported across the field.

result: Prior VAR2CSA subunit vaccines (PAMVAC and PRIMVAC) failed to induce broadly neutralizing antibodies, showing activity primarily against homologous parasites. Similarly, VAR2CSA fragments failed to purify broadly neutralizing activity from multigravidae sera.
evaluation: Claims C4, C29-C34 are well-supported by citations to clinical trials (Mordmüller et al., 2019; Sirima et al., 2020) and prior work (Doritchamou et al., 2016). These establish the rationale for the current study's focus on full-length VAR2CSA ectodomains.

result: Sequential affinity purification on five VAR2CSA ectodomain variants yielded ~386.1 µg of VAR2CSA-specific IgG (~0.7% of total IgG), with the first two variants (NF54 and 7G8) capturing 76% of the total purified IgG.
evaluation: Claims C6, C37, C38 are directly supported by experimental data in Table 1, showing quantitative yields from the purification procedure. The calculations are straightforward and the data are clearly presented.

result: Depletion of IgG on five VAR2CSA variants successfully removed reactivity to those variants and substantially reduced cross-reactivity to heterologous variants (M920, M200101) and maternal isolates, as measured by ELISA and flow cytometry.
evaluation: Claims C39-C43 are supported by experimental data in Figures 2A, 2B, and supplementary figures. The depletion is demonstrated by loss of reactivity in post-depletion samples. The identification of WF12 encoding 7G8 VAR2CSA (C42) is supported by citation and sequence analysis.

result: Depletion of IgG on five VAR2CSA variants significantly reduced CSA-binding inhibition activity against all tested isolates, with reduction ranging from 45% to 87%. The pre-depletion total IgG showed >65% inhibition against most isolates (except FCR3 at 33%).
evaluation: Claims C44-C47, C10 are supported by functional assay data in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3. The quantitative measurements of inhibition activity before and after depletion are clearly presented. The inference that cross-inhibitory IgG to maternal isolates was depleted (C47) is reasonable given the data.

result: VAR2CSA-purified IgG exhibited cross-reactivity to different variants by ELISA, with the degree of cross-reactivity dropping substantially after the first purification. NF54-purified IgG showed the highest reactivity to all variants, while M. Camp-purified IgG (last in series) showed no cross-reactivity to earlier variants.
evaluation: Claims C48-C52, C7 are supported by ELISA data in Figure 3A. The pattern of decreasing cross-reactivity with successive purifications is clearly demonstrated. Each variant purified some homologous reactivity, supporting both strain-transcending and strain-specific antibody populations.

result: By flow cytometry, NF54-purified IgG showed the greatest breadth and highest level of reactivity to IE surface of all parasites including maternal isolates. Subsequent purifications (7G8, FCR3, M. Camp, HB3) showed progressively lower surface reactivity and cross-reactivity.
evaluation: Claims C54-C58 are supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3B showing MFI values. The pattern is consistent with ELISA results, demonstrating that the first purification captures the most broadly reactive antibodies. Complete depletion of homologous reactivity is confirmed.

result: NF54-purified IgG contained the largest fraction of CSA-binding inhibitory activity with normalized BIA (nBIA) >50% against all isolates and ~100% for most, including maternal isolates. Blocking was achieved at IgG concentrations as low as 10 µg/mL. Subsequent purifications showed lower but detectable cross-inhibition activity.
evaluation: Claims C59-C65, C8, C9 are supported by functional assay data in Figures 4A-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2. The normalization approach is reasonable, and the data clearly show that the first purification captures most broadly neutralizing activity. The titration data (C61) supports potency at low concentrations.

result: In a second independent experiment with permutated antigen order, M. Camp-purified IgG (now first in series) exhibited the highest cross-reactivity to heterologous VAR2CSA variants and strongly cross-inhibited binding of M. Camp, FCR3, and NF54 parasites to CSA, consistent with the first experiment.
evaluation: Claims C66-C69 are supported by data in Figure 5A-E. This replication with different antigen order strengthens the conclusion that the first variant used captures broadly neutralizing antibodies regardless of which variant is used first. This is a critical control.

result: A single VAR2CSA ectodomain variant displays conserved epitopes targeted by neutralizing antibodies shared by multiple parasite strains. IgG purified on a single variant captured the bulk of strain-transcending IE reactivity and CSA-binding inhibition activity, demonstrating that VAR2CSA is the major target of functional antibodies and that the full-length ectodomain displays both variant-specific and shared epitopes.
evaluation: Claims C11, C70, C71, C85, C89-C91, C99-C101 represent the major conclusions of the study. They are well-supported by the convergent evidence from both purification experiments showing that: (1) the first variant captures most broadly neutralizing activity, (2) depletion on five variants removes most functional activity, and (3) the pattern replicates with different antigen order. The data strongly support these conclusions.

result: Removal of IgG specific to five VAR2CSA ectodomain variants significantly reduced/abolished IE-surface reactivity and CSA-binding inhibition activity of total IgG. VAR2CSA-purified IgG exhibited strong cross-reactivity to all isolates, with IgG purified on the first variant showing the highest cross-reactivity.
evaluation: Claims C76, C80-C83 summarize key findings supported by Figures 2 and 3. The depletion and purification data converge to show that VAR2CSA-specific antibodies account for most functional activity, and that broadly reactive antibodies are captured on the first variant used.

result: The findings suggest that a broadly effective PM vaccine can be achieved with a limited number of VAR2CSA variants, potentially even a single variant, though challenges in vaccine development remain including possible interference from non-functional epitopes.
evaluation: Claims C12, C86, C94, C102 are speculative conclusions about vaccine development based on the antibody purification data. While the data support that naturally acquired antibodies to a single variant can be broadly neutralizing, this does not directly demonstrate that immunization with a single variant will induce such antibodies. The authors appropriately acknowledge challenges (C94, C95), but the vaccine efficacy claim requires actual immunization studies.

result: Functional antibodies may target conformational epitopes on full-length VAR2CSA (exemplified by PAM1.4 monoclonal antibody). While other invariant proteins are expressed by placental parasites, antibodies to these proteins appear to have limited blocking activity, though synergistic effects cannot be excluded. Cross-reactive antibodies could result from both linear and conformational epitopes.
evaluation: Claims C35, C72-C75, C77-C78, C103-C105 are supported by citations (particularly Barfod et al., 2007 for PAM1.4) and are reasonable interpretations of the data. The speculation about limited activity of non-VAR2CSA antibodies (C77) is appropriately cautious. The statement about conformational epitopes (C103-C104) is well-supported by prior work.

result: The parasite isolates tested represent geographically diverse origins including South America (7G8), South East Asia (M. Camp), East Africa (M0736), and West Africa (NF54, M2022170, M2001190).
evaluation: Claim C84 is supported by the description of parasite origins and is consistent with known geographical distributions of these strains. This diversity strengthens the conclusions about broad cross-reactivity.

result: Prior preclinical studies with full-length VAR2CSA in rodents showed strong homologous but not heterologous functional activity. Antibody responses to VAR2CSA may differ between species or based on exposure type (vaccine vs. natural infection), including differences in antibody glycosylation.
evaluation: Claims C87-C88, C92-C93 are supported by citations (Khunrae et al., 2010; Avril et al., 2011; Larsen et al., 2021). These provide important context for interpreting the differences between naturally acquired human antibodies and vaccine-induced antibodies in animal models.

result: Speculative interpretations suggest that higher OD values for NF54 purification may indicate greater abundance/affinity of cross-reactive vs. variant-specific IgG. Non-functional epitopes may interfere with optimal antibody responses, and the flexible arm of VAR2CSA may mask functional epitopes. Manufacturing challenges may require novel technologies like mRNA vaccines.
evaluation: Claims C53, C95-C98 are speculative statements about mechanisms and future directions. While plausible, they lack direct experimental support in this study. C53 is a reasonable interpretation but alternative explanations exist. C95-C96 are possibilities that would require additional experiments to test. C97-C98 are forward-looking statements about vaccine development.

result: Naturally acquired antibodies target both variant-specific and conserved epitopes and exhibit broadly neutralizing anti-adhesion activity. Antibodies from multigravid women recognize placenta-binding parasites from diverse geographical origins.
evaluation: Claims C5, C36, C79 represent established knowledge supported by multiple citations (Fried and Duffy, 1998; Ricke et al., 2000; Ndam et al., 2015). These provide the scientific rationale for the study.

result: Methods description: Plasma pools were prepared from multigravid women in the IMEP study in Mali. Recombinant VAR2CSA ectodomains from seven strains were expressed in mammalian cells. Variable numbers of passages were needed for complete IgG depletion.
evaluation: Claims C106-C109 describe the materials and methods, supported by citations (Fried et al., 2018; Renn et al., 2021) and methodological details. These are adequately documented for reproducibility.
